title: Cipher and Safehouse Again
premise: Kestrel Iversen is hired to quietly investigate the disappearance of a charter flight's records, only to discover the plane never landed and its manifest names people officially dead for years. The vanished flight is a rehearsal for a larger 'accident' being engineered by a syndicate that erases inconvenient histories — including Kestrel's own. As Kestrel races to decode the cipher left by a dead whistleblower, they uncover that their survival as a contractor was bought with a buried betrayal. In the end, Kestrel stops the attack at a coastal summit, exposes the syndicate's ledger, and chooses to publish their own erased past rather than keep surviving on silence.
about_author: Wendell Pemberton is the pen name of a former aviation insurance investigator who spent a decade reconstructing flights no one wanted remembered. They write from a farmhouse whose previous owner left behind a locked filing cabinet they have never opened.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Kestrel Iversen takes a discreet retainer from a grieving sister whose brother's charter flight has vanished from every database mid-air. POV: Kestrel. The beat is quiet unease — the case pays too well and asks too few questions.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Digging through airport contacts, Kestrel finds the passenger list: six names, all belonging to people who died years ago. POV: Kestrel, with an intercut of the sister, Mara, receiving a threatening call. The emotional beat shifts from curiosity to dread.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: After someone torches Kestrel's office, an old handler stashes them in a decommissioned safehouse with rules: no phones, no names, no history. POV: Kestrel. The beat is claustrophobic trust — Kestrel realizes the handler knew about the flight already.

chapters.title: Cipher in the Ceiling
chapters.summary: Behind the safehouse panels, Kestrel finds a dead whistleblower's coded notebook linking the ghost passengers to a syndicate called the Ledger. POV alternates between Kestrel decoding and a flashback to the whistleblower's final night. Beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for an Accident
chapters.summary: Decrypted files reveal the vanished flight was a test run for a staged crash targeting a coastal security summit in nine days. POV: Kestrel briefing Mara, who refuses to walk away. Beat: reluctant alliance hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Kestrel infiltrates a Ledger archive and finds their own file — proof their career was manufactured to bury a betrayal they don't remember committing. POV: Kestrel, unraveling. Beat: the ground gives way beneath identity itself.

chapters.title: Nine Days, Six Names
chapters.summary: With the handler compromised and Mara missing, Kestrel trades a forged copy of the cipher to buy time, suspecting the buyer will kill them anyway. POV splits between Kestrel and Mara held in a safehouse of her own. Beat: sacrifice and self-loathing.

chapters.title: Descent Vector
chapters.summary: Kestrel traces the sabotage team to a private airfield where the 'accident' aircraft is being prepped, and confronts the handler, who confesses to authoring Kestrel's false memory. POV: Kestrel. Beat: fury transmuted into cold clarity.

chapters.title: The Summit Sky
chapters.summary: Climax: Kestrel and rescued Mara breach the summit's air-traffic override, forcing the sabotaged aircraft down short of the target while broadcasting the Ledger's ledger live. POV: rapid alternation. Beat: terror, then release.

chapters.title: Everything I Buried
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Kestrel publishes their own erased file alongside the syndicate's, ending the price-of-survival bargain forever. Mara rebuilds her brother's true record; the safehouse is sealed. POV: Kestrel, quiet. Beat: costly peace, honestly earned.
